To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the power consumption of the conventional binary-weighted architecture is smaller than other architectures and that the linearity requirements of the attenuating-capacitor architecture impose much larger capacitances to each unit cell such that the power consumption is larger.

, for a given linearity, the power consumption of the attenuating capacitor architecture is higher than that of conventional binary-weighted architecture, and that, for a fixed power budget, the attenuating capacitor structure has a lower linearity compared to the conventional binary-weighted structure.

(1) the power consumption of the conventional binary-weighted structure is smaller than the other structures, (2) the power consumption is not the only factor in choosing the architecture, and (3) the power consumption and INL/DNL are not the only factors to choose between the structures, but also other factors such as the area, the number of switches, the number of capacitors, and the number of bits should be considered as well.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the power consumption and linearity of capacitors used in the DACs of successive approximation ADCs.
the power consumption and linearity of capacitative DACs employed in SA- ADCs, and the results are useful for designers in choosing the best DAC architecture and optimizing it for their application.
the analysis of the power consumption and linearity of capacitors in the DACs used in SA-ADC architectures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in terms of linearity, the power consumption of the conventional binary-weighted structure is the least, and the one with attenuating capacitors is the worst, while in terms of power consumption, the binary-weighted structure consumes the most power, and the one employing attenuating capaci-tances the least.
binary-weighted structures are the most power-efficient and the most linear among the three considered architectures.
the conventional binary-weighted DAC is the best choice in terms of the power consumption and linearity for SA-ADCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binary-weighted architecture is the best choice for low-power SA-ADCs.
the power consumption of a capacitive DAC is mainly dominated by the total capacitance while the linearity is dominated by the parasitic capacitances.
the power consumption and linearity requirements impose a lower limit on the size of the smallest unit capacitor in a DAC, which is a function of the resolution and the conversion speed of the ADC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to achieve the best linearity, the unit capacitors should be designed to be as small as possible and the power consumption can be reduced by increasing the number of parallel branches.

, although the power consumption and linearity requirements of SA-ADCs impose larger capacitance values than conventional binary weighted DACs, the power consumption can be significantly reduced by using an appropriate architecture and the proposed analysis can be used for that.
the parasitics are not negligible in the analysis and design of the SA-ADCs.
